summary: This bill makes the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) a mandatory spending program, ensuring it receives necessary funding each fiscal year starting in 2026, rather than relying on annual appropriations.

scores.thoughts: This bill mandates funding for the WIC program by appropriating 'such sums as are necessary' from the Treasury for fiscal year 2026 and each succeeding fiscal year, effectively increasing government spending by making the program an entitlement rather than subject to annual appropriations.

The bill converts the WIC program, which provides nutritional support to women, infants, and children, into a mandatory spending program, thereby expanding and securing a key component of the social safety net.

The bill converts WIC from discretionary to mandatory spending by appropriating 'such sums as are necessary' automatically each year, locking in higher federal outlays without any offsets or revenue measures. This directly increases baseline spending and tends to enlarge deficits to protect the program.
